title: CSV Coordinate Bounding Box: Instant Extent
description: Get the S/W/N/E extent of a coordinate CSV with the CSV Coordinate Bounding Box — viewport and API bbox numbers without desktop GIS. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a five-city US file (New York to Los Angeles) returns west −118.2437, south 29.7604, east −74.0060, north 41.8781 — a box 1,347 km tall that frames the whole dataset.
quick_answer: The CSV Coordinate Bounding Box computes the geographic extent of a coordinate spreadsheet — the westernmost, southernmost, easternmost and northernmost values across every valid row. Paste the CSV and read the S/W/N/E bounds: the numbers map viewports, API bbox parameters and first-pass dataset QA all ask for.

Overpass and places APIs want (S, W, N, E). Compute your data’s own extent here to sanity-check the query you are about to run.
A US-only file whose box reaches longitude +40 has a swapped or unsigned row hiding in it — the box is the cheapest lie detector in geospatial work.
Exports clip to extents. Knowing the true box before choosing tiles or shards prevents both gaps and gigabytes of empty ocean.

New York, Chicago, Los Angeles, Houston and Denver: W −118.2437 (Los Angeles), S 29.7604 (Houston), E −74.0060 (New York), N 41.8781 (Chicago). South-to-north the box spans 12.1177° of latitude — about 1,347 km of ground.

popular_table.note: Invalid rows are excluded from the extent — which is why a box can look sane while rows silently fail; pair the box with validation counts when QA matters.

faq: The latitude and longitude columns your file declares — pick them as the tool presents them. Mislabelled columns produce a box that is obviously wrong, which is its own diagnostic.
Rows without parseable coordinates do not move the edges. The tool reports the extent of the valid data; validators on this site report the invalid rows themselves.
A file spanning ±180° yields a box the long way around (min −179, max +179 reads as nearly world-wide). Pacific datasets need seam-aware handling — the box honestly reports the naive extent.
Can I get the centre too?
The box’s midpoint is a rough centre; the CSV Coordinate Centroid Calculator computes the mean of the points themselves — different numbers, different meanings.
A swapped file’s box often shows an impossible latitude edge (beyond ±90 in longitude clothing) or a mirrored location — the box is the fastest swap detector there is.
The box is in degrees (that is what APIs and viewports eat); the summary translates spans into kilometres for human reading.
A degenerate box — all four edges meet at the point. Valid, and the map will need a default zoom to show anything.
